h1:
Nakhon Sawan to Lopburi
Monkey Town Meets Old City
intro: Nakhon Sawan and Lopburi sit about 130 km apart. Drive south on Highway 1, then Highway 11, and you're there in roughly 2 hours — close enough to string together into one relaxed road trip. Nakhon Sawan gives you Thailand's largest freshwater lake and the source of the Chao Phraya River, while Lopburi is an old Khmer-to-Ayutthaya town where monkeys really do roam the streets. We've built this as a 3-day, 2-night plan running north to south, with a day-by-day timeline so you can see exactly what to do each day and where to stop and eat.

blocks.html: This route suits anyone with their own car or a rental, because spots like Bueng Boraphet and Pa Sak Jolasid Dam sit outside town and are awkward to reach by public transport. If you only want Lopburi's old town, though, the historic sites are all within walking distance — hop off the train and you can cover them on foot. The main route is dead simple: take Highway 1 from Nakhon Sawan, then turn onto Highway 11 around the Tak Fa–Khok Samrong stretch into Lopburi town. The drive runs through flat plains and rice fields, easy going, with gas stations and roadside coffee stops along the way.

blocks.text: Route overview and how to plan your days

blocks.html: The idea behind the plan is to use Nakhon Sawan as your starting point, knocking out Pak Nam Pho and Bueng Boraphet first since the highlights are scattered around the city. Once those are done, you shift down to Lopburi, the historical highlight of the trip. Lopburi's old-town sites are clustered close together and walkable, so you can cover them comfortably in a single day. That leaves the last day open for Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, or the sunflower fields if you come in the cool season. The driving legs between stages aren't long — the longest drive is the day you move from Nakhon Sawan down to Lopburi.

items: Day 1 — Pak Nam Pho, the Pasan landmark at the source of the Chao Phraya, then Bueng Boraphet in the afternoon, overnight in Nakhon Sawan
Day 2 — drive down to Lopburi in the morning, walk the old town: Phra Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan, King Narai's Palace, overnight in Lopburi
Day 3 — Pa Sak Jolasid Dam or the sunflower fields (cool season) before heading home

blocks.title: Rough distances
blocks.html: Nakhon Sawan to Lopburi is about 130 km on Highway 1 (Phahonyothin) via Tak Fa, around 2 hours. From Lopburi town to Pa Sak Jolasid Dam (Phatthana Nikhom district) is roughly 50 km — budget half a day there and back.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Pak Nam Pho + Bueng Boraphet

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Source of the Chao Phraya, then out to Thailand's biggest lake

items.activity: Start at Pasan, the landmark marking the source of the Chao Phraya River, out on the Ko Yom headland at Pak Nam Pho, where the Ping and Nan rivers meet
items.note: The white riverside architecture photographs beautifully, and in the early morning the sun is still soft and the walk is pleasant

items.activity: Walk old Pak Nam Pho, taking in the old shophouses and the Chao Pho–Chao Mae Pak Nam Pho shrine, the city's old Chinese community
items.note: Nakhon Sawan has deep Chinese-community roots, which you can see in its shrines and its food

items.activity: Lunch around Pak Nam Pho — try a famous spot for fish-ball noodles made with clown knifefish
items.note: Pak Nam Pho is known for bouncy, freshly made clown knifefish balls, with long-running shops that have been open for decades

items.activity: Drive out to Bueng Boraphet, the largest freshwater lake in the country
items.note: About 10 km from town, with several viewpoints and boat piers along the lake's edge

items.activity: Visit the Bueng Boraphet Aquarium, walking the long fish tunnel and seeing over a hundred species of freshwater fish
items.note: Open roughly 09:00–17:00. Good with kids and a nice way to dodge the afternoon heat

items.activity: Take a boat out on the lake to see the waterbirds in the evening light — arrange a boat at the lakeside pier
items.note: Boat fares are charged per boat or per person depending on the spot, so ask the price before you board

items.activity: Head back into town for dinner at a riverside market or a freshwater-fish restaurant
items.note: Evenings along the Chao Phraya have breezy riverside spots with an easy, relaxed mood

blocks.title: Bird-watching season at Bueng Boraphet
blocks.html: November to February is migratory-bird season. Come at dawn or in the evening to catch the most waterbirds. If you're serious about birding, swap in a boat trip on the morning of Day 1 instead.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Down to Lopburi, walking the monkey old town

blocks.html: This is the highlight of the trip. Drive from Nakhon Sawan down to Lopburi in the morning, then walk the cluster of historic sites in the town center, which are close enough to cover on foot. Lopburi is a town where crab-eating macaques really do live right in the center, especially around Phra Prang Sam Yot and San Phra Kan. It's part of the town's charm, but you'll want to keep a bit of an eye on whatever's in your hands and your bag.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Khmer-to-Ayutthaya history downtown, plus the resident monkeys

items.activity: Leave Nakhon Sawan on Highway 1 (Phahonyothin) via Tak Fa into Lopburi town
items.note: About 130 km, roughly 2 hours, with room to stop for roadside coffee

items.activity: Check in to a place in Lopburi's old town, then walk over to Phra Prang Sam Yot, three Khmer towers in a row in the Bayon style
items.note: Open roughly 08:30–18:00, with admission in the tens to fifty baht. This is a monkey hotspot, so mind what's in your hands

items.activity: Cross to San Phra Kan opposite — an old shrine on a Khmer-era laterite base, with monkeys living densely around here
items.note: San Phra Kan and Phra Prang Sam Yot are home turf for the town's monkeys and the image most people have of Lopburi

items.activity: Lunch in town — try a famous bowl of Lopburi tom yum noodles
items.note: Tom yum noodles are a local specialty, and the long-running shops are in the old-town area

items.activity: Walk Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat, opposite Lopburi train station, with an old central prang and ruined halls from several eras
items.note: Another standout historic site blending Khmer and Ayutthaya styles, walkable from the train station

items.activity: Enter King Narai's Palace (Phra Narai Ratchaniwet), a palace from King Narai's reign with a museum inside
items.note: Open roughly 08:30–16:00, closed Monday–Tuesday, with admission in the tens of baht for Thais. Check the day before you go

items.activity: Stop by Ban Vichayen (the Ambassador's Residence), the ruins of a building from King Narai's reign nearby
items.note: Not far from King Narai's Palace, a short walk or quick drive away, and it closes in the evening too

items.activity: Dinner in town at an evening market or a riverside spot in Lopburi
items.note: If you're into river prawns and river fish, there are riverside restaurants outside town to choose from as well

blocks.title: Mind the monkeys a little
blocks.html: Around Phra Prang Sam Yot and San Phra Kan the monkeys are plentiful and used to people. Don't carry food bags, drinks, or loose glasses or hats in your hands. Tuck valuables into a zipped bag and you'll have a fun visit with no drama.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Pa Sak Dam or the sunflower fields

blocks.html: Pick the last day to suit the season. If you come in the cool season (November to February), the Phatthana Nikhom district has big sunflower fields in bloom. Out of season, head to Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, a large earthfill reservoir whose floating railway over the water at Khok Salung is a highlight. Both spots are out toward Phatthana Nikhom district, not far from Lopburi town.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Closing the trip with the dam's natural side

items.activity: Leave Lopburi town heading toward Phatthana Nikhom district for Pa Sak Jolasid Dam
items.note: About 50 km, easy driving on an out-of-town road with rice fields on both sides

items.activity: See Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, the dam-crest viewpoint and the Pa Sak Basin Museum
items.note: A large earthfill reservoir, wide-open and breezy

items.activity: Look out for the floating railway at Khok Salung, where the train line runs across the reservoir
items.note: The floating tourist train usually runs around November to January — check the railway schedule first

items.activity: Lunch at a restaurant by the dam, with freshwater fish from the reservoir on the menu
items.note: There are local restaurants around the dam — try grilled fish or tom yum fish

items.activity: In the cool season, stop at the sunflower fields on the Phatthana Nikhom side for photos of the yellow blooms before heading home
items.note: Sunflowers bloom around November to February. Skip this stop if you're out of season

items.activity: Pick up some Lopburi souvenirs, then start the journey home
items.note: If you're looping back to Bangkok, continue on Highway 1 down to Saraburi onto Highway 1 or the motorway

blocks.html: This plan has you sleeping 2 nights. We'd suggest the first night in Nakhon Sawan around Pak Nam Pho — a big town with plenty of hotels and food, close to Bueng Boraphet. For the second night, stay in Lopburi town: pick the old-town area to walk to the historic sites easily, or the train-station area, which has hotels and a market nearby.

items.name: Stay in Pak Nam Pho, Nakhon Sawan (Night 1)
items.blurb: City center, lots of restaurants, close to Bueng Boraphet and Pasan — easy to get out and about

items.name: Stay in Lopburi old town (Night 2)
items.blurb: Walk to Phra Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan and King Narai's Palace — sightsee in the morning without driving

blocks.text: Eats you shouldn't miss along the way

items.name: Pak Nam Pho clown knifefish-ball noodles
items.blurb: A Nakhon Sawan signature — bouncy, freshly made clown knifefish balls. The famous shops around Pak Nam Pho have been open for decades, and some also do tod mun and fried snacks. Good for breakfast or lunch before you head out.

items.name: Lopburi tom yum noodles
items.blurb: Lopburi's signature dish — a punchy, sour-and-spicy tom yum broth with pork or mixed seafood. Several long-running shops sit in the old-town area, making it a lunch that pairs well with walking the historic sites.

items.name: Lopburi plain noodle soup
items.blurb: A clear, well-rounded noodle soup with a choice of pork or beef and various noodle types. Some shops also do steak at night. This is where Lopburi locals actually eat.

items.name: River prawns and river fish by the water in Lopburi
items.blurb: Riverside restaurants outside Lopburi serve fresh river prawns and river fish. Try grilled prawns or salt-crusted grilled snakehead — a long, lingering dinner soaking up the riverside mood.

items.name: Pak Nam Pho congee and rice soup
items.blurb: Pak Nam Pho is a Chinese-community area, so breakfast staples like minced-pork congee and rice soup are easy to find all over the neighborhood. Ideal for a morning meal before heading to Bueng Boraphet.

items.name: Freshwater fish by Pa Sak Dam
items.blurb: Around Pa Sak Jolasid Dam, local restaurants cook freshwater fish straight from the reservoir. Try grilled fish or tom yum fish — a lunch that pairs nicely with the dam views.

items.name: Nakhon Sawan riverside market
items.blurb: Evening and night eats from riverside stalls, from made-to-order dishes to rad na, fried oysters and desserts. Easy on the wallet.

blocks.text: Tips to make the trip smoother

items: King Narai's Palace closes Mon–Tue — schedule Day 2 to land on Wed–Sun if you mean to go in, and always check the day beforehand
Mind the monkeys in Lopburi — don't carry food bags or loose items around Phra Prang Sam Yot and San Phra Kan
Sunflower season, Nov–Feb — come now and you get both the sunflower fields and migratory-bird season at Bueng Boraphet, the best fit overall
Start early — both Bueng Boraphet and Lopburi's old town are cooler in the morning and less crowded

faq.q: Is Nakhon Sawan far from Lopburi? How many hours to drive?
faq.a: About 130 km on Highway 1 (Phahonyothin) via Tak Fa, roughly 2 hours of driving. The route runs across flat plains and is easy going, with gas stations and roadside coffee stops along the way.

faq.q: How many days does this trip need?
faq.a: This plan is built for 3 days and 2 nights, which fits nicely — you get Pak Nam Pho and Bueng Boraphet on the Nakhon Sawan side, plus Lopburi's old town and Pa Sak Dam. If you're short on time, drop the last day and squeeze it into 2 days by covering Lopburi town in a single day.

faq.q: Are the Lopburi monkeys aggressive? Is it dangerous?
faq.a: The monkeys around Phra Prang Sam Yot and San Phra Kan are used to people and like to grab food. As long as you don't carry food bags or loose items in your hands and keep valuables in a zipped bag, it's a safe visit — and it's a charm of the town you won't find elsewhere.

faq.q: Can you do this route without your own car?
faq.a: Lopburi's old town is easy to do by train and on foot, since the historic sites are near the train station. But Bueng Boraphet and Pa Sak Dam are out of town and awkward by public transport. If you want to cover the whole route, renting a car or having your own is the smoother option.

faq.q: What month do Lopburi's sunflowers bloom?
faq.a: Lopburi's sunflowers bloom around November to February each year. The Phatthana Nikhom side near Pa Sak Dam plants big fields, and this window is the best fit for the trip since you get both the flower fields and migratory-bird season at Bueng Boraphet.
